text:
Florida was the better team by the numbers and still lost by three. The Panthers had 3.19 expected goals against Minnesota's 4.7, but nearly all of Minnesota's edge was late and lopsided: 2.94 in the third period alone. At even strength the teams were almost level (1.99 to 1.85), and the simulations gave FLA a 56 percent chance of deserving the win. The gap between play and result came down to Jesper Wallstedt, who faced 3.19 expected goals, allowed one and saved about 2.19 more than an average goalie would have.

Kirill Kaprizov did the rest. He scored three times and added an assist, including a power-play snap shot in the first period that made it 2-0 and a second-period goal just 2:42 after Matthew Tkachuk had cut the lead to 2-1. Matt Boldy opened the scoring 53 seconds in on a snap shot, a 5 percent chance that went in anyway. Kaprizov's team-high 3.52 expected goals while on the ice, against only 0.46 allowed, shows he was driving play and not just finishing.

The third period decided it, and Minnesota's last goal was the cleanest of the night. Kaprizov's wrist shot at 18:56 carried a 55 percent chance of scoring, a fitting capper for a period in which MIN outchanced FLA 2.94 to 1.47. Jacob Markstrom was close to par, giving up three on 2.84 expected, so this wasn't a goaltending collapse for Florida. The Panthers got five power plays and scored on none of them, while Minnesota cashed in on its one real opportunity of three.
